condition: paroxysmal positional vertigo provoked on rolling over in bed
level_rationale: Five days of brief 15-second positional spinning vertigo with mild nausea triggered by rolling over in bed is a classic uncomplicated peripheral positional vertigo presentation for an outpatient doctor visit and repositioning maneuver, whereas accompanying double vision is a central brainstem or posterior-circulation red flag requiring immediate emergency evaluation.

reference_facts.text: Episodes are triggered by rolling over in bed
Each episode of spinning dizziness lasts 15 seconds
Episodes are accompanied by mild nausea

texts.medical: I am 48 years old and for 5 days rolling over in bed has provoked 15 second rotational vertigo with mild nausea so I should see a
texts.everyday: I am 48 years old and for 5 days rolling over in bed has brought on 15 second spinning giddiness with mild nausea so I should see a
texts.medical_paraphrase: I am a 48 year old with 5 days of 15 second episodes of rotational vertigo and mild nausea triggered by rolling over in bed so I should see a
texts.everyday_paraphrase: I am a 48 year old and over the past 5 days turning over in bed triggers 15 second bouts of spinning giddiness and mild nausea so I should see a
texts.changed_fact: I am 48 years old and for 5 days rolling over in bed has brought on 15 second spinning giddiness with double vision so I should see a

swap_note: Single continuous 5-word vs 6-word span swap after 'I am 48 years old and for 5 days rolling over in bed has ' and before ' with mild nausea so I should see a'.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Indian English dialect lexicon swap ('rotational vertigo' vs 'spinning giddiness', retained in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact accompanying-symptom escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Isolates Indian English 'spinning giddiness' against 'rotational vertigo' in a 5-word vs 6-word span with 8 identical trailing tokens ('with mild nausea so I should see a'). Swapping only atomic fact f5 from mild nausea to double vision introduces a classic central brainstem diplopia red flag that shifts care from outpatient doctor evaluation (level 2) to emergency care (level 4) with zero stated negatives.
